newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Hoogovens outlines Boel investment plan.
newsitem.headline: Hoogovens outlines Boel investment plan.

text.p: Dutch steel maker Hoogovens, which is setting up a 50/50 joint venture with Belgian steel firm Usines Gustave Boel (UGB), said on Friday investments at UGB would focus on re-training and on UGB's equipment.

"There will be two types of investment, one in personnel and one in the installations," Aad van der Velden, a member of Hoogoven's executive committee, told a news conference at which the two companies announced the formal signing of the deal.

Under the deal 4.25 billion francs of fresh funds will be injected into loss-making, privately-owned UGB via a new holding company to be owned 50/50 by Hoogovens and UGB. The holding will own 100 percent of UGB and of (Fabrique de Fer de Mauberge.

Provided in a mixture of cash and subordinated loans, this includes 2.25 billion from Hoogovens, 500 million from the Walloon Region's SWS steel investment company and the rest from UGB's present shareholders.
"We will invest in organisation, the personnel and in training, to modernise it," Van der Velden said.

There would also be investment in the technology of UGB's cold and hot rolling mills at the company's La Louviere site, south west of Brussels, and the addition of a cost-cutting coal and oxygen injection option to the electrical arc furnace.
As a result of the restructuring the number of workers at La Louviere is being cut to 1,300 from about 2,000.
The new Hoogovens-UGB alliance will have annual capacity of 500,000 tonnes of steel a year from the electrical furnace.

For long and flat products capacity will include 950,000 to one million tonnes of hot and cold laminated coils, 200,000 tonnes of rolling semi-finished products on contract, and 250,000 tonnes of steel wire.
Flat galvanised and painted steel capacity will be 300,000 tonnes of coils, sheets and profiles.
